chapter.title: Conditional and filter annotators
chapter.para: The examples use the text The dog barks. It naps., tokenized on whitespace.

section.title: Writing a custom annotator
section.para: The annotator below defines its own key in its own code, reads the token layer, and provides one integer annotation per token; the analyzer's build-time validation guarantees a tokenizer ran earlier:
Because the key declares the value type, the values come back as numbers without a cast; for the text above the five values are 3, 3, 6, 2, 5, each on its token's span:
section.programlisting: List<Annotation<Integer>> lengths = document.get(TOKEN_LENGTHS); int firstTokenLength = lengths.get(0).value(); // 3, for "The" at [0..3)
section.para: Required layers must be present, but they may be empty: an empty token layer yields the annotator's provided layers present but empty, so a pipeline degrades gracefully on documents without content. An absent required layer is rejected with an IllegalArgumentException naming the layer, because a missing pipeline stage is an assembly error, not an empty document. DocumentAnnotators.requireLayers performs exactly that rejection, including the null check on the document, and is what the toolkit's own adapters use.

section.title: Conditional and filter annotators
section.para: ConditionalAnnotator selects a pipeline stage from a predicate over the document. The two-argument form runs its delegate when the predicate is true. When it is false, the delegate's output layers are added empty:
The three-argument form selects between explicit true and false branches. Both branches must provide the same layers. The wrapper declares the union of their required layers:
FilterAnnotator copies matching annotations to a distinct layer without modifying the source layer:
A filter function receives an annotation and can also receive the document, so it can compare a normalized value with the original text at the annotation span:

Offsets use UTF-16 units, while capitalization is tested on Unicode code points. For example, the Deseret capital letter U+10400 starts the Java string "\uD801\uDC00lice" and occupies UTF-16 offsets 0 to 2. Empty spans and spans containing only part of that character do not pass the filter.

Both wrappers reject a document that lacks a required layer, with an IllegalArgumentException naming the layer: the filter needs its source layer, and the conditional needs the declared inputs of every branch. For the filter above, a document without the token-length layer produces:
section.programlisting: filter.annotate(Document.of("The dog barks. It naps.")); // IllegalArgumentException: document lacks the required layer token-lengths<Integer>
